name: Schloss Fernsteinsee
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Fernsteinsee on the Fern Pass sits by an emerald mountain lake featuring the Sigmundsburg island fortress, boating, diving depths, and Mieming range vistas.
preis: Shoreline pathways freely accessible; paddle/rowing boat rentals approx. €12-16/hour; diving requires permit
oeffnungszeiten: Grounds and trails open year-round; hotel and restaurant facilities operate May to October
beschreibung:
Überblick

The storied Schloss Fernsteinsee complex rests at an elevation of 984 metres directly beside the winding Fern Pass road within the municipality of Nassereith in the Tyrolean Oberland. Nestled amidst fragrant conifer woodlands beneath the sheer limestone faces of the Mieming Range, this grand castle hotel and its emerald lake constitute one of Western Austria's most evocative romantic landmarks. Covering roughly 18 hectares with depths plunging to 17 metres, the crystal-clear body of water was created by a prehistoric landslide and exhibits exceptional underwater clarity reaching up to 20 metres. Submerged tree skeletons and vibrant aquatic moss formations render the lake an internationally acclaimed destination for alpine freshwater scuba divers. Crowning an islet in the lake's heart stand the mystic ruins of Sigmundsburg Castle, erected in the 15th century by Archduke Sigmund the Rich. The stately Schloss Fernstein exudes historic hospitality along the famed Roman route Via Claudia Augusta.

Route & Anforderungen

Walking the perimeter of Lake Fernsteinsee is a tranquil pleasure for sightseers. The 2.5-kilometre circular trail requires roughly 45 to 60 minutes of gentle stroll with minimal gradients. The route meanders over mossy forest floor, wooden footbridges, and flat shoreline paths, unlocking scenic vistas of the castle turrets and the Sigmundsburg islet. Standard sneakers or light walking shoes are entirely adequate. Hikers desiring a longer trek can trace the historic Via Claudia Augusta toward Nassereith or climb to the Fern Pass summit (approx. 1.5 hours). The loop features a few tree roots but remains broad and safe.

Besuch & Anreise

Access is directly via the federal Fernpassstraße B179 between Nassereith and Biberwier, where pay parking is situated adjacent to the castle grounds. Rail passengers travel to Imst-Pitztal or Telfs-Pfaffenhofen stations and catch regular VVT regional coaches over the Fern Pass, alighting at the 'Fernsteinsee Schloss' stop.

Tipps

Rent a vintage rowing boat or swan pedal craft at the lakeside dock to glide quietly around the forested Sigmundsburg island. Early morning hours offer mirrored reflections of the Mieming peaks across tranquil water, followed by artisanal pastries on the castle café terrace.
